caption: Hot bacon fat is poured into a glass jar straight from the fridge, and the fat begins to set where it touches the cold glass.

sa.check: A glass jar that reads as cold: frost or condensation on it.
Hot fat is poured into the jar.
The fat begins to set where it touches the glass.
Solid white fat forms at the jar's walls.
The poured fat is clear and runny.
The order is pour, set at the walls, spread inward.

pc.expect: The setting runs one way: the white grows from the cold glass inward and the fat's surface stops sloshing.
pc.fail: The white creeps back to the glass leaving the fat clear again; or the set fat turns runny with nothing heating it; or the white appears in the middle first and works out to the glass; or the fat sets and melts in turn.

pc.expect: The change from clear to white happens in the fat itself, at the cold glass, and spreads through it.
pc.fail: The jar's glass turns white rather than the fat; or the white appears in the pan before the fat is poured; or the white fades back to clear while the jar is still cold; or the label on the jar changes rather than the fat.

pc.expect: The fat falls downward into the jar and lies level in it, its surface flat while the jar stands upright.
pc.fail: The fat climbs the jar's wall above its level and stays; or the stream travels upward from the pan; or the fat's surface tilts and stays tilted with the jar upright; or fat lifts out of the jar's mouth.

pc.expect: The hot fat is a thin liquid that pours and sloshes and the set fat is a soft opaque solid that keeps its shape when the jar is moved.
pc.fail: The set fat sloshes when the jar is tilted; or the fat sets into a glassy solid that cracks; or the fat stretches like dough as it is poured; or the liquid fat stands in a heap above its level.

pc.expect: One jar and one pour; the fat that goes in stays in.
pc.fail: The fat's level drops with none poured out; or fat appears in the jar with none pouring in; or the fat passes through the jar's wall; or a second jar appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The jar's label, the pan and the counter stay the same.
pc.fail: The label changes; or the pan changes shape; or items on the counter rearrange.
